title: New Jersey's 12th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New Jersey's 12th Congressional District is an open-seat race to succeed retiring Democratic U.S. Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, who has served since 2015. The district covers parts of Mercer, Middlesex, Somerset, and Union counties and is considered a safe Democratic seat, with a Cook Political Report rating of Solid D. The Democratic nominee is Dr. Adam Hamawy, a former U.S. Army combat surgeon and plastic surgeon who won a crowded 13-candidate primary on June 2, 2026. He will face Republican Gregg Mele, an attorney and frequent candidate who ran unopposed in the Republican primary. The general election will be held on November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No independent general election polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The district is rated Solid D by Cook Political Report.

candidates.name: Adam Hamawy
candidates.summary: Dr. Adam Hamawy is a plastic and reconstructive surgeon, former U.S. Army lieutenant colonel, and combat trauma surgeon who served in Iraq and helped save the life of U.S. Sen. Tammy Duckworth. He won the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, with 27.4% of the vote in a 13-candidate field. His campaign focuses on Medicare for All, reducing military spending, and addressing affordability for working families.

candidates.name: Gregg Mele
candidates.summary: Gregg Mele is an attorney, businessman, and graduate-level professor who has run for public office seven times across multiple districts as an Independent, Libertarian, and Republican. He practices corporate law, contracts, securities, real estate, and estate planning at Mele & Associates, LLC. His campaign focuses on border security, lowering taxes, school choice, parental rights in education, and reducing government dependence.
